column1: # Everything not listed here keeps its default, and the job fails on any FAIL-level alert. A rule
# is only moved to IGNORE with the reason written down, because an ignored finding that nobody
# can justify later is indistinguishable from a vulnerability nobody noticed.
# Review this file when.4's header list changes.

column3: Incomplete cache-control on public pages is deliberate: the guest microcache caches them on purpose, and logged-in responses do send Cache-Control: private with Vary: Cookie.
Information disclosure in suspicious comments: template comments explain markup, carry no data.
Modern web application: the islands architecture is server-rendered HTML plus small scripts, which this heuristic flags by design.

column1: # --- Checked by the test suite rather than by a passive scan --------------------------------

column3: Absence of anti-CSRF tokens: ZAP cannot see the per-session token, which is checked on every state-changing request and covered by the e2e suite.
Loosely scoped cookie: the session cookie uses the __Host- prefix, which ZAP's heuristic reads as loosely scoped.

column1: # --- Must never regress: these are the headers requires -------------------------------

column3: Web browser XSS protection not enabled.
Cross-domain JavaScript source file inclusion -- scripts load only from our own origin.
Missing anti-clickjacking header (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options).
Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
Strict-Transport-Security header missing on an https deployment.
Content-Security-Policy header missing.
Permissions-Policy header missing.
Cross-domain misconfiguration (CORS is off by default,).
CSP: wildcard or unsafe directive -- the policy is strict.
Timestamp disclosure.
Weak authentication method.
Reflected cross-site scripting.
Persistent cross-site scripting.
SQL injection.
Remote OS command injection.
Application error disclosure -- errors are problem+json without internals.
